rubric.meaning: relevant means PLAUSIBLY CONNECTED to the subject, as the person grades it
rubric.2: something on the card -- a stated topic, a paper title, a role -- sits in the search's subject area or a close neighbour
rubric.1: the subject shows only as skill tags (e.g. Stack Overflow tags), with no papers, role or bio
rubric.0: nothing on the card is in the subject's area, or the card is empty
rubric.derived_from: the person's 14 grades in calibration rounds 2 and 3; the rule reproduces all 14, but was fitted to them, so that is not validation

superseded.work_shows_it: the 2026-10-02 'the work shows it' rubric, under which round 3 did not pass

post_fix_check.why: the recall and location fixes of 2026-10-03 put 11 people in Seekr's top ten whom the labels never covered; Claude graded them, not blind (it knew they were Seekr's), and stated those grades in chat on 2026-10-03
post_fix_check.control_rule: per query, the first unseen pool card ordered by sha256('seekr relevance pool 2026-09-30|postfix 2026-10-04|' + card id)

measures: share of the 11 entrants the person grades 2, and 1 or 2: the precision of what the fixes added
exact agreement person vs Claude on the 11 (non-blind on Claude's side) and on the 7 controls
top-ten share graded 2 over all 191 places, with the person's grades for the 11
the controls are one per query the entrants come from: six
post_fix_check.caveat: the person saw Claude's grades for the 11 described in chat on 2026-10-03, so their grading of those 11 is not fully blind to Claude's; the controls are

result.entrant_agreement: 6/11 exact, none 0 against 2 (Claude's side not blind)
result.control_agreement: 3/6 exact, one 0 against 2: Kae Nemoto (quantum computing, Japan) for 'machine learning researchers in India', Claude 0, person 2
result.reading: The fixes held precision: the eleven people they added grade like the rest of the top ten. The labels are noisier than the validation suggested: across the two blind checks (validation 7/10, these controls 3/6) the person and the labels agree exactly on 10 of 16 cards, with one 0 against 2. Where they differ the labels are more generous on neighbouring fields (ALS for dementia, LHC physics for cosmology) and the person applies the place rule unevenly (Preskill, not in India, graded 2; V. Sharma, not in India, graded 1). Read every score against these labels as +-0.1, not to the third decimal.

rubric_v2.person_grades: the person's own grades (calibration rounds 2 and 3, validation, post-fix check) stand as given: they are the standard this rubric writes down
plan: relabel every pooled card under this rubric; cards the person graded keep the person's grade

accept if >= 8/10 exact and none 0 against 2; otherwise report and do not score against them
if accepted, re-run scripts/score_relevance_labels.py and update the README
